summary: Shift project scope to a legal, browser-based (online) 3D car racing/traffic-jam game with a single vehicle, with an aim to publish on the Google Play Store.
architectural_notes: Game scope: single vehicle only (legal constraint).
Target: runs online in a web browser; consider packaging path for Google Play Store (e.g., WebView/TWA) if required.
Compliance requirement: keep implementation and monetization approach fully legal/Play-policy compliant.
Gameplay access policy: enforce online-only play (block offline usage even if installed as a PWA).
Do not share or distribute any Caffeine preview/admin URLs containing #caffeineAdminToken; use a public production URL or a token-free share link for users.
Support mobile touch UI controls: on-screen Left/Right buttons to steer the single player vehicle.

Ensure mobile-first responsive layout: game canvas should occupy visible viewport and controls must not push gameplay off-screen; avoid scroll/zoom dependence by anchoring HUD and sizing canvas appropriately.
Gameplay constraint: only the player vehicle should exist in the scene; no AI/traffic vehicles ahead/behind.
Track layout constraint: create exactly one road/track path for the single player vehicle (avoid multiple parallel roads/lanes).
Quality/polish goal: make the experience feel like a Play Store–ready app (high-quality, app-like UI/UX and visuals).
known_issues: User shared a Caffeine URL containing #caffeineAdminToken (sensitive). Must rotate/revoke token and provide a public/token-free link before sharing.
Caffeine build/deploy failed due to an internal configuration issue; may require Caffeine team support to resolve.
Download/Install ("Downloading") flow is currently not working correctly; user reports downloads are failing and wants it to work when shared with friends.
On mobile, only the top control buttons are visible; the road/track and car are not visible without scrolling/zooming (layout/viewport/camera framing issue).
User reports other cars/vehicles are appearing ahead/behind; needs to be removed so only the single player vehicle is present.
Player car model/texture is facing the wrong direction (orientation flipped from intended).
Road/track currently appears as multiple (three) roads/lanes; must be simplified to a single road/track.
imageRequirements:
## Required Images
- Racing car texture with bold stripes and a simple number panel (race-car-texture.dim_1024x512.png)

existing_features.title: Create a mobile-first single-page app that acts as an Android-installable wrapper for the existing website https://sites.google.com/view/saanrewards/home, with a clear primary action to open the site in the same tab (default) and an alternate action to open it in a new tab.
Add Progressive Web App (PWA) support so the app can be installed on Android from Chrome (Add to Home Screen), including a web app manifest, app icons, and a minimal offline fallback screen.

Add a consistent visual theme for the app (colors, typography, spacing, and component styling) and apply it across all screens; choose a distinct style appropriate for a rewards/loyalty app and avoid a blue/purple default palette.
Add a simple “About / Help” area that explains what the app does (opens the Saan Rewards website) and provides the website URL as a tappable link.
Replace the current Saan Rewards website-wrapper landing page + iframe flow with a browser-playable “Traffic Jam” car game experience as the primary app content.

Implement a simple 3D Traffic Jam gameplay loop with exactly one player vehicle: the player controls a single car, navigates through traffic/jam obstacles, and can restart after a collision/game over.

Add an in-app Help/About panel for the Traffic Jam game in English that explains: how to play, that it runs online in the browser, and a clear note that the game uses original assets and is intended to be legally compliant (no copyrighted/unauthorized content).
Update PWA metadata to match the Traffic Jam game (app name, description, categories, and any shortcuts) so the installed experience represents the game rather than Saan Rewards.
Generate and use new PWA app icons for the Traffic Jam game and store them as static assets under frontend/public/assets/generated, updating the manifest to reference the new filenames.
Enforce an online-only restriction so the Traffic Jam game cannot be played without an active internet connection (offline play must be blocked).

Modify the PWA service worker behavior to prevent the app/game from functioning offline (do not cache game assets for offline use), while still allowing a dedicated offline page to appear when navigation occurs without network connectivity.
Update the in-app Help/About content to explicitly state (in English) that Traffic Jam requires an active internet connection and does not support offline play.

Add an app-like Start / Home screen (before gameplay begins) with clear actions in English: “Play”, “How to Install”, and “Share Link”. The Start screen must be mobile-first and should make the experience feel like a real app (clean layout, strong primary CTA, minimal distractions).

Implement an in-app PWA install flow: detect when the app is installable (via the browser install prompt) and show an “Install App” button in the Start / Home screen (and/or in the Help dialog). If installation is not available, show simple English instructions for installing on Android Chrome (Menu → “Add to Home screen”).

Add a safe “Share Link” feature that copies a public URL without any `#caffeineAdminToken=...` fragment. If the current URL contains `caffeineAdminToken` in the hash, the app must (a) avoid displaying it anywhere, and (b) copy a sanitized link that removes the full hash fragment from the shared URL.
Add a brief security note (English, user-facing) on the Share screen/section: “Do not share admin links that contain tokens.” This note must not include or echo any token value.
Add the user-provided uploaded image as a hero/banner on the Start / Home screen and display the game name "Traffic Jam" over/above the image in a clear, readable style (English text).

Make the Start / Home screen include a clearly labeled "Download" action that triggers the existing PWA install flow (or shows install instructions when install prompting is not available). Use English user-facing text.
Update the Start / Home screen hero/banner image to use the newly uploaded car image instead of the previous hero image, keeping all user-facing text in English.
Update the in-game player vehicle visuals so the player car uses the newly uploaded car image as its appearance (texture/sprite/mesh material), while keeping gameplay logic unchanged.
Fix the Start / Home screen “Download” action so users can reliably install the app as a PWA on Android Chrome and are never blocked by incorrect “Installed” detection.

Make the shared link flow friend-friendly by ensuring the Share UI provides a reliable share/copy method and clear next-step guidance that the recipient should tap “Download” to install (English text only).

Add a visible in-progress state for the Start / Home screen “Download” action so users get clear feedback while the PWA install prompt is being triggered and while the app is waiting for the user’s response.
Track and expose an install-flow status in the PWA install hook and/or Start / Home screen so the UI can reliably render the “Downloading/Installing” progress state without race conditions.

Update the 3D Traffic Jam environment to include a distinct, attractive road/track that clearly defines where the player car drives (a dedicated road surface with edges/shoulders), replacing the current plain flat road appearance while keeping gameplay logic unchanged.

Add visible greenery/plant decoration along both sides of the road throughout the forward direction of travel, using original/procedural geometry (no third-party copyrighted models) and ensuring the plants do not block lanes or cause collisions.

Make the mobile on-screen Left and Right buttons reliably steer the player car in-game by ensuring press-and-hold sets the shared control state and release/cancel always clears it, across mobile touch and pointer input.

Update the touch control event handling to use robust mobile-safe events (pointer events and/or touch start/end + touch cancel) for Left/Right (and Brake if present), without changing gameplay logic other than making the controls responsive.

Fix the mobile game layout so the 3D game view (road/track and player car) is always visible without requiring the user to scroll or zoom, even when the on-screen control buttons (Left/Brake/Right) are shown.
Adjust the in-game camera framing (start-of-game and during normal play) so the player car and a meaningful section of the road ahead are clearly visible on mobile in portrait orientation.

Ensure the road/track environment includes clearly visible greenery/plant decoration along both the left and right sides of the road throughout the forward direction of travel, and confirm plants do not block lanes or create unintended collisions.

Add a simple in-game visual driving demonstration so the user can immediately understand how the car moves on the road (e.g., a brief automatic forward roll and/or slight left-right preview at the beginning), with English user-facing text if any labels are shown.
Fix the game viewport/layout so the 3D Canvas always has a non-zero height and is fully visible on mobile without scrolling, including when the on-screen touch controls are shown.
Fix any React Three Fiber scene issues that can prevent rendering (including incorrect instanced-mesh usage for roadside plants) so the scene reliably renders without runtime errors.
Add a user-facing fallback when the 3D scene cannot render (e.g., WebGL unavailable or scene initialization error), using English text and providing a clear retry action.

Update the Traffic Jam gameplay scene so that no other vehicles/cars appear ahead of or behind the player at any time; the only car in the scene must be the player’s car. If obstacles remain, they must be non-vehicle objects (e.g., barriers) and must not be visually represented as cars.

Update the in-game player vehicle rendering so the player car looks like a real 3D car (e.g., distinct body + cabin + wheels), instead of appearing like a flat image/texture on a simple box, while keeping all gameplay logic (controls, lane movement, collisions, scoring, speed) unchanged.

Fix the player car’s facing/orientation so the car front (“mouth”) points to the intended forward driving direction in the 3D scene (correct the current flipped direction) without changing the car’s geometry details.

Change the Traffic Jam track/road gameplay from a 3-lane setup to a single-road path: remove the three-lane logic/markers and ensure the car drives on only one road (no multiple parallel roads/lanes).

Update player steering behavior to work correctly with the single-road track: Left/Right controls should move the car within the single road boundaries (clamped), rather than lane-switching across multiple lanes.

Improve the overall UI/UX presentation so the Traffic Jam PWA feels like a high-quality, Play Store–ready app, with consistent styling across the Start/Home screen, Help/About dialogs, Share/Install flows, and in-game HUD (while keeping all user-facing text in English).

Upgrade visual styling of key interactive elements to feel production-quality: primary/secondary buttons (Play/Download/Share), touch control buttons, dialog surfaces, and HUD elements (score and game-over overlay), including improved states (hover/pressed/disabled/loading) and consistent shadows/borders.

Add lightweight app-like motion polish (subtle transitions/animations) for screen and dialog interactions (e.g., opening Help/About, Share, Install instructions) and for game state overlays (game over / restart) without impacting game performance on mobile.

Replace the current primary app experience (Traffic Jam game) with a mobile-first single-page website wrapper for https://sites.google.com/view/saanrewards/home, with a clear primary action to open the website in the same tab and an alternate action to open it in a new tab.
Update PWA metadata so the installed experience represents the Saan Rewards website wrapper (app name, description, categories, shortcuts if any) rather than Traffic Jam.
Ensure the app supports Android installation as a PWA from Chrome (Add to Home screen) and includes a minimal offline fallback page for navigations when the device is offline.
Add a simple in-app About / Help area that explains the app opens the Saan Rewards website and provides the website URL as a tappable link.

Update the in-game player vehicle visuals to look like a small, best-looking race car (sport/racing style) instead of a basic/local-looking car, without changing any gameplay logic (controls, speed, scoring, collisions, obstacle behavior).

Replace the player car’s current texture usage with a new racing-style texture asset and apply it to the player car materials so the car looks like a race car (e.g., bold color blocks/stripes/number panel), keeping assets original and stored under frontend/public/assets/generated.

new_feature_requests.summary: Build an Android app for the website https://sites.google.com/view/saanrewards/home (Saan Rewards).
Create an online (browser-based) 3D car racing / traffic-jam game with only one vehicle, designed to be legally compliant and suitable for eventual Google Play Store release.
Add an online-only restriction so the game cannot be played offline (require an active internet connection; prevent public/offline play).
Add a “Download” button so users can download/install the app/game (user requested a downloading button).
Replace the previous hero/banner image with the newly provided car image, and use that same car asset as the in-game player vehicle.
Add a small progress indicator to the Download/Downloading flow (show download/install progress feedback to the user).
Create a distinct, attractive road/track environment for the car to drive on, with plants/greenery placed along both sides of the road.
Add mobile on-screen Left/Right buttons to control the player car (touch controls mapped to steering).

Fix the game screen layout/camera so the road/track and player car are always visible on mobile (not hidden below the on-screen buttons); ensure the canvas/viewport fits correctly without requiring scroll/zoom.

Add a simple in-game visual guidance/demo so the user can clearly see how the car drives on the track (e.g., start-of-game camera framing and/or brief auto-move/preview), without changing the single-vehicle gameplay rules.
Remove all other vehicles/traffic cars so only the single player car is present (no cars ahead or behind).
Replace the current player car that looks like a flat image/texture with a more realistic 3D car model/mesh (make the car look ‘real’).
Fix the player car orientation/facing direction (car ‘mouth/front’ should face the intended side; current edit flipped it incorrectly).
Change the environment/track so there is only one road/track path for the car (not three roads/lanes); the car should drive only on that single road.
Improve overall app/game presentation to look high-quality and Play Store–ready (app-like UI/UX polish, production-quality visuals and layout).
Replace the current player car ("local" car) with a small, best-looking race car style/model to improve the game’s visuals.
